title: Encorafenib and binimetinib for advanced BRAF-mutated melanoma
context_label: NCCP 00563: adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600 mutation.
purpose: Encorafenib and binimetinib block two points in the BRAF-MEK growth pathway to help control eligible advanced melanoma. The team reviews response, symptoms and side effects to decide whether the treatment continues.
schedule_summary: Take encorafenib once daily and binimetinib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, continuously unless the team tells you to hold them. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerable. A 28-day review calendar does not mean a routine break or a fixed total number of cycles.
scope_note: NCCP 00563: adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600 mutation.

timeline_note: This calendar shows the pattern. Your team supplies actual dates, prescribed doses and any hold or restart instructions.
safety_note: The prescribed dose, treatment decision and local urgent-contact plan take priority. Call 112 or 999 for severe breathing difficulty, severe chest pain, collapse, a new seizure, sudden weakness or speech difficulty, or uncontrolled bleeding. Follow your oncology unit’s written urgent-contact plan for other new or worsening symptoms; do not wait for the next appointment.
teachback: Can you explain your treatment setting, medicine schedule, next tests, the symptoms that need urgent advice and the number you would call?
consent_support: Discuss the exact diagnosis, treatment intent, expected benefits and uncertainty, suitable alternatives, the regimen-specific risks and monitoring, fertility and pregnancy precautions, and practical burdens. Confirm the treatment phase and route. This guide supports the conversation and does not replace individual consent.
urgent_extra: Contact the team promptly for new visual symptoms, chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, faintness, severe muscle pain or weakness, dark urine, bleeding, severe rash, persistent diarrhoea or severe abdominal pain. Do not continue one medicine at an unchanged dose if the other has been held without a specific team instruction. Report markedly reduced urine, persistent vomiting, new muscle cramps or weakness, or palpitations promptly; the team may need to check salts, kidney function and tumour lysis risk.

agents.name: Encorafenib
agents.explanation: Encorafenib blocks altered BRAF signalling in eligible melanoma. Binimetinib acts at a different step in the same growth pathway. Each medicine retains its own dosing and safety instructions.
agents.watch: A change to binimetinib can change the encorafenib plan. Have interactions checked and avoid grapefruit.
risks: Skin reactions and new skin tumours
Nausea, vomiting, fatigue and joint pain

agents.name: Binimetinib
agents.explanation: Binimetinib inhibits MEK proteins in the growth-signalling pathway. Alongside effects on cancer cells, it can affect muscle, heart and retinal tissue. The prescribed blood and heart checks and prompt review of new eye symptoms help detect these effects.
agents.watch: Report vision change or muscle pain/weakness promptly; keep CK, kidney and heart checks even when you feel well.

passport_visit_note: Record the actual date, treatment received, any hold, important symptom and the next check. A review visit is not automatically a medicine dose or a completed cycle.
anatomy_note: The established anatomical illustration links body areas to the full regimen-specific descriptions. A body location helps explain possible effects; it does not diagnose the cause of a symptom or indicate its frequency.
anatomy: Fatigue and headache can occur. Fever, marked weakness, dizziness or new neurological symptoms needs advice; do not assume it is a harmless drug effect.
Blurred vision, spots, altered colour vision or eye pain needs prompt assessment. Retinal problems may occur with binimetinib.
Keep ECG and heart-pumping checks. Report palpitations, fainting, swollen ankles or new breathlessness; severe chest pain is an emergency.
Report new growths or changes in existing spots and attend skin checks. Severe rash, blistering or peeling needs urgent help.
Liver changes may have no early symptoms, so attend monthly tests. Report yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or upper-abdominal pain.
Kidney tests accompany CK monitoring. Reduced urine, dehydration or dark urine with muscle symptoms needs urgent advice.
CK can rise before or with muscle injury. Report muscle pain, weakness or dark urine, and keep the planned blood tests.
Nausea and diarrhoea may occur. Persistent vomiting, inability to drink, severe abdominal pain, black stools or bleeding needs assessment.

phases.label: Continuous oral treatment
cycles: Encorafenib daily + binimetinib twice daily, continuously; reviewed regularly.
phases.detail: Take encorafenib once daily and binimetinib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, continuously unless the team tells you to hold them. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerable. A 28-day review calendar does not mean a routine break or a fixed total number of cycles.

chronology_notes.title: Timing note 1
chronology_notes.text: Take encorafenib once daily and binimetinib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, continuously unless the team tells you to hold them. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerable. A 28-day review calendar does not mean a routine break or a fixed total number of cycles.

chronology_notes.title: Timing note 2
chronology_notes.text: For a missed encorafenib dose, take it only if more than 12 hours remain before the next dose. For binimetinib, do not take a missed dose if fewer than six hours remain before the next; ask the pharmacist if timing is uncertain. Do not double doses. If either medicine is vomited, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose unless the team advises otherwise.

chronology_notes.title: Timing note 3
chronology_notes.text: Temporary holds may need coordinated changes to both medicines; no patient-led dose adjustment.

chronology_notes.title: Timing note 4
chronology_notes.text: The regimen is advanced melanoma; it is not an adjuvant treatment template.

chronology_notes.title: Timing note 5
chronology_notes.text: No trial outcome percentage is assigned without confirming the exact population, comparison and follow-up.

chronology_notes.title: Timing note 6
chronology_notes.text: Tumour lysis syndrome is a source-listed risk, especially with high tumour burden, kidney problems or dehydration. The team decides whether extra hydration and blood checks are needed.

administration_text: The usual method is to swallow the prescribed capsules/tablets whole with water, with or without food. If swallowing is difficult, ask the pharmacist for the source-permitted preparation: Braftovi capsules may be opened into about 20 mL of apple puree for immediate use, and Mektovi 15 mg tablets may be dispersed in about 10 mL of water, orange juice or apple juice, taken immediately, followed by a further 10 mL rinse. Do not assume this applies to other tablet strengths or improvise a preparation. Keep doses at consistent times. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, and have all medicines and supplements checked.
monitoring_summary: Confirm BRAF V600 and treatment setting. Full blood count, kidney/liver tests, creatine kinase (CK) and creatinine, blood pressure, ECG, a heart-pumping assessment by echo or MUGA, and skin examination. Blood count, kidney/liver tests monthly. CK and creatinine monthly for the first six months, then as indicated. ECG at four weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose changes; heart-pumping assessment every three months. Skin assessment every 60 days, head/neck examination every three months and chest CT every six months. Response scans follow the individual plan. Continue skin surveillance for six months after stopping as specified by the regimen. Agree continuing symptom/organ checks, the next melanoma assessment and medicine-specific pregnancy precautions.

support.title: An individual symptom plan
support.text: Ask which anti-sickness or other symptom medicines are prescribed, when to take them and when to call if they do not help. Do not start a borrowed medicine or alter treatment to manage a side effect yourself.

support.title: Your urgent contacts
support.text: Keep your actual oncology, out-of-hours and pharmacy contacts on the wallet card. Example numbers on a template must be replaced before you use it.

support.title: Pregnancy and fertility precautions
support.text: Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least one month after the last dose. Hormonal contraception needs an additional or alternative barrier method because interactions can reduce effectiveness. Discuss fertility beforehand and follow the team’s breastfeeding instructions. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

support.title: Eating, activity and practical help
support.text: Let the team know if cramps, altered taste or poor appetite make eating or moving difficult. Ask for practical food and activity advice that fits your symptoms and any other illness.

support.title: Hydration and tumour lysis assessment
support.text: The team checks whether tumour burden, kidney problems or dehydration call for additional precautions and blood tests. Keep the individual fluid plan; do not force fluids if you have a restriction. Report reduced urine, persistent vomiting or marked weakness promptly.

sections.title: Appointments and supply
sections.text: Plan blood tests, travel and medicine collection in advance. If you need an interpreter or someone to help at home, tell the team before the appointment.

sections.title: Paper copies and contact information

evidence.intro: Discuss the evidence for your diagnosis, tumour test results and treatment setting.
evidence.population: NCCP 00563: adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600 mutation.
evidence.interpretation: Ask which outcomes matter in your setting and what benefit is realistic for you. No survival percentage from another regimen, dose combination or disease setting is assigned here.

Your team explains the evidence that applies to this treatment plan and the uncertainty for you as an individual.

chapters.title: Understanding your diagnosis and treatment goal
chapters.intro: Use these questions with your own pathology report and agreed treatment plan.

items.title: What the diagnosis says
items.text: Record the original melanoma site and pathology findings. Breslow thickness and ulceration describe features of the skin tumour; stage describes its extent. Melanoma arising in the eye or a mucosal surface may need a different pathway.

items.title: BRAF and other tumour tests
items.text: A BRAF V600 result identifies whether the targeted medicines in this plan can act on the tumour. Keep the laboratory result and date. A tumour change is not, on its own, evidence of an inherited condition.

items.title: Surgery, radiotherapy and medicine have different roles
items.text: Ask whether medicine is intended to reduce recurrence after complete surgery or control cancer that remains. Add any operation or radiotherapy to the plan with its own purpose, timing and risks.

items.title: Stage and response are different
items.text: Stage describes the extent of disease. Response describes a change in measurable cancer during treatment. After complete removal there may be no visible tumour to measure; follow-up then looks for recurrence and treatment effects.

items.title: A new skin change still needs review
items.text: Report a new or changing mole, a sore that persists, a new lump or an unexplained symptom. A photo or a good response in one area cannot rule out a separate problem.

chapters.title: Your medicines and the overall plan
chapters.intro: Encorafenib and binimetinib block two points in the BRAF-MEK growth pathway to help control eligible advanced melanoma. The team reviews response, symptoms and side effects to decide whether the treatment continues.

items.title: The schedule in this setting
items.text: Take encorafenib once daily and binimetinib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, continuously unless the team tells you to hold them. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerable. A 28-day review calendar does not mean a routine break or a fixed total number of cycles.

items.title: How the treatment works
items.text: Encorafenib blocks the BRAF V600 growth signal in eligible melanoma cells. Binimetinib acts further down the same pathway. They have different dose schedules and different safety decisions, so the prescription for one must not be assumed to apply to the other. Binimetinib inhibits MEK in the cell-growth pathway. It can also affect normal muscle, heart and retinal tissues. CK blood tests, heart checks and prompt reporting of eye or muscle changes help the team identify problems before they become more serious.

items.title: The role of earlier or later treatment
items.text: Ask how the medicine fits with previous or planned local treatment. The timing of an operation, radiotherapy and a tablet course should be written in one agreed plan.

items.title: Pauses and stopping
items.text: A safety pause is an active treatment decision. Record which medicine is paused, the reason, the tests or recovery needed and who may authorise restarting. Do not restart from an old prescription or reset the history when a new phase begins.

chapters.title: Taking treatment and preparing for visits
chapters.intro: Keep the written medicine plan beside this guide; it records your own dose and dates.

items.title: Taking or receiving the medicine
items.text: The usual method is to swallow the prescribed capsules/tablets whole with water, with or without food. If swallowing is difficult, ask the pharmacist for the source-permitted preparation: Braftovi capsules may be opened into about 20 mL of apple puree for immediate use, and Mektovi 15 mg tablets may be dispersed in about 10 mL of water, orange juice or apple juice, taken immediately, followed by a further 10 mL rinse. Do not assume this applies to other tablet strengths or improvise a preparation. Keep doses at consistent times. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, and have all medicines and supplements checked.

items.title: Missed, vomited or held treatment
items.text: For a missed encorafenib dose, take it only if more than 12 hours remain before the next dose. For binimetinib, do not take a missed dose if fewer than six hours remain before the next; ask the pharmacist if timing is uncertain. Do not double doses. If either medicine is vomited, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose unless the team advises otherwise.

items.title: Other medicines and supplements
items.text: Show the pharmacist a current list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, herbal products and supplements. Include anticoagulants, heart medicines, steroids and recent antibiotics. Check before adding, stopping or changing anything; an apparently harmless product can alter treatment or confuse a symptom assessment.

items.title: Practical preparation
items.text: Bring your medicine list, allergy information and questions. Tell the team about practical problems with travel, swallowing, wound care or remembering doses before treatment starts.

chapters.title: Tests: what is required and what each result means
chapters.intro: Safety tests, tumour tests and response scans answer different questions.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: Confirm BRAF V600 and treatment setting. Full blood count, kidney/liver tests, creatine kinase (CK) and creatinine, blood pressure, ECG, a heart-pumping assessment by echo or MUGA, and skin examination.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: Blood count, kidney/liver tests monthly. CK and creatinine monthly for the first six months, then as indicated. ECG at four weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose changes; heart-pumping assessment every three months. Skin assessment every 60 days, head/neck examination every three months and chest CT every six months. Response scans follow the individual plan.

items.title: Scans and tumour markers
items.text: Ask the team to write the next assessment and who will arrange it. Bloods used to monitor kidneys, liver, hormones or muscle are not automatically measures of cancer response. There is no universal tumour-marker blood schedule for these skin-cancer regimens; a scan or extra blood test is requested for a specific clinical reason.

items.title: After a pause or finish
items.text: Continue skin surveillance for six months after stopping as specified by the regimen. Agree continuing symptom/organ checks, the next melanoma assessment and medicine-specific pregnancy precautions.

items.title: Getting the result
items.text: Keep a named contact for bookings and results. If an expected appointment or result is missing, call that service; do not take silence as confirmation that everything is complete.

chapters.title: What to expect between visits
chapters.intro: You can feel well and still need the planned checks. New symptoms deserve attention even on a day without an appointment.

items.title: Your usual pattern
items.text: Record the start and change in symptoms, temperature if advised, bowel pattern, drinking, urine and the effect on normal tasks. A simple few-line record is enough. Use it to describe a change rather than trying to grade or diagnose a toxicity yourself.

items.title: When to call
items.text: Contact the team promptly for new visual symptoms, chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, faintness, severe muscle pain or weakness, dark urine, bleeding, severe rash, persistent diarrhoea or severe abdominal pain. Do not continue one medicine at an unchanged dose if the other has been held without a specific team instruction. Report markedly reduced urine, persistent vomiting, new muscle cramps or weakness, or palpitations promptly; the team may need to check salts, kidney function and tumour lysis risk.

items.title: Eating, drinking and activity
items.text: Report nausea, mouth discomfort, diarrhoea or weight loss before they make eating and drinking difficult. The team can adjust symptom support and arrange dietitian or rehabilitation advice.

items.title: A held dose and a new phase
items.text: For a missed encorafenib dose, take it only if more than 12 hours remain before the next dose. For binimetinib, do not take a missed dose if fewer than six hours remain before the next; ask the pharmacist if timing is uncertain. Do not double doses. If either medicine is vomited, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose unless the team advises otherwise.

chapters.title: Skin checks, sun protection and optional photographs
chapters.intro: This complements clinical assessment and does not replace it.

items.title: Protect your skin
items.text: Protect exposed skin with clothing, a hat and shade. Use broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher and reapply as directed. Avoid sunbeds. Cloudy weather does not remove ultraviolet exposure.

items.title: Know the pattern of your skin
items.text: Ask the team to show you how to check your skin and treated area. Use a mirror or a helper for areas you cannot see. Report a new lump, a changing lesion or a sore that does not heal.

items.title: Photographs are optional
items.text: A private, dated photograph can help describe a change if your team finds it useful. Keep the lighting and size reference consistent. Photographs support a discussion; they do not replace examination and need not be uploaded.

items.title: Wounds, nails and sensitive skin
items.text: Follow the wound and skin-care instructions for the treated area. Ask before adding a cream or remedy. Increasing redness, discharge, pain, bleeding or difficulty using the area needs assessment.

chapters.title: Pregnancy, fertility and protecting others
chapters.intro: Discuss these precautions before treatment even if pregnancy is not currently planned.

items.title: Medicine-specific precautions
items.text: Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least one month after the last dose. Hormonal contraception needs an additional or alternative barrier method because interactions can reduce effectiveness. Discuss fertility beforehand and follow the team’s breastfeeding instructions. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

items.title: Planning ahead
items.text: Ask early about fertility preservation, sexual health and symptoms affecting intimacy. Tell the team about any chance of pregnancy, breastfeeding or a partner’s pregnancy so that the correct medicine-specific advice can be given. Keep the precautions and their end dates in the written plan.

items.title: Safe handling and supply
items.text: Do not share anticancer medicines. Keep oral medicines in their original labelled packaging, away from children and anyone who could take them accidentally. Return unused medicines to the supplying pharmacy and follow its handling advice. A treatment hold does not remove pregnancy precautions.

chapters.title: Questions, decisions and practical support
chapters.intro: Your priorities and the burden of treatment belong in the discussion.

items.title: Benefits and uncertainties
items.text: Ask what outcome this treatment aims to improve for your diagnosis and what alternatives exist. Results from a study group help a discussion but cannot promise your own result.

items.title: Alternatives and review points
items.text: Agree the next decision point and what would make the plan change. Ask about other suitable treatments, trials and symptom care. Support for comfort and function can continue alongside cancer treatment.

items.title: Help with daily life
items.text: Tell the team what is hardest in daily life: travel, work, caring duties, costs, sleep or confidence. Ask who can help and how to contact them.

items.title: Shared understanding
items.text: Before going home, check that you can describe your medicine schedule, next tests and urgent-contact route. Ask for an interpreter, larger print or a supporter if that would help.

chapters.title: Follow-up and your continuing record
chapters.intro: Keep this record when treatment is paused, changed or completed.

items.title: Your follow-up plan
items.text: Your stage, symptoms and treatment determine follow-up. Write down the skin and lymph-node checks, any body or brain scans and the service arranging them. Confirm your own dates with the team.

items.title: Continuing medicine precautions
items.text: Continue skin surveillance for six months after stopping as specified by the regimen. Agree continuing symptom/organ checks, the next melanoma assessment and medicine-specific pregnancy precautions.

items.title: Treatment summary for other clinicians
items.text: Record the medicines and last dates, important reactions, any long-term hormone replacement or steroid taper, and the responsible oncology contact. Show this information in urgent care and to other specialists. A different treatment phase does not erase earlier toxicity.

items.title: The complete paper version
items.text: Use this handbook as your paper record. Keep the current schedule, medicines, tests and contacts together, and replace outdated pages after a change. The matching QR link is optional.

For binimetinib, do not take a missed dose if fewer than six hours remain before the next; ask the pharmacist if timing is uncertain. Do not double doses. questions.q: Can I use this without a smartphone?
questions.a: Yes. The full handbook, three-page summary and wallet card are printable. The QR code is optional; keep actual contacts and written appointments on the paper copy.
